title: Read a versioned Bazaar string
summary: Read the latest or an exact immutable string version and list an ID's retained versions through the CLI or an in-process Rust reader.

consumers.statement: Local programs use the in-process bazaar::api Rust API. People and authorized agents use the Bazaar CLI.

preconditions.statement: The selected database is initialized and uses Bazaar schema one. Its path is absolute, with a private regular parent directory and a private regular database file.

data_semantics.statement: Raw string operations preserve opaque UTF-8 without parsing, normalization, templating, merging, or execution. Empty content is valid. IDs are nonempty exact strings with caller-owned meaning. The separate bazaar.prompts.prepare feature owns prompt text preparation.

identity_and_units.statement: An ID and its positive integer version identify one immutable record. Versions start at one independently for each ID. There are no timestamps or measurement units.

access.statement: The current user's filesystem permissions protect state. Rust readers open SQLite read-only and expose no writes. CLI dispatch separately attempts metadata-only Chancery usage recording; direct API reads do not.

operational_limits.statement: SQLite waits up to five seconds for lock contention. Content and complete version lists are held in memory. There is no service-level latency, content-size, or throughput guarantee. A connection is not shared concurrently between threads; callers can open independent handles.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Database schema one, CLI output schema one, API types, provider release, and capability versions have separate identities. Unsupported or foreign databases fail without migration.

reliances.statement: Core string operations use local SQLite and files only. No external service, model, or installed catalog is a runtime dependency.

inputs.statement: Get accepts a nonempty exact ID and an optional positive version. History accepts one nonempty exact ID. The global --database option selects an absolute database path.

outputs.statement: Get returns id, version, and exact content. History returns the ID and every retained version number in descending order. Rust methods return Record or Vec<i64> with typed errors. CLI reads use readable text by default. Global --json selects the existing schema-one JSON results. Text get includes complete content; history lists every retained version. Operational errors exit 1: text on stderr by default, or schema-one ok:false with error.detail on stdout with --json. Syntax errors remain Clap text on stderr with exit 2. Record has id: String, version: i64, and content: String; bazaar::api::Result<T> uses the public typed Error.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Latest means the greatest committed version for the ID visible to that SELECT. An exact get selects one immutable record. History selects every committed version of the ID visible to its SELECT. Separate calls do not share a snapshot; no timestamps are emitted.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Reads never initialize, repair, migrate, append, or delete Bazaar state. A missing ID or version returns NotFound. A Reader opened earlier observes newly committed versions in later queries.

use_when: A caller needs a workflow's stored text or configuration string.
A caller needs to inspect an earlier version or an ID's version numbers.
do_not_use_when: The caller wants to render a template, parse model configuration, execute an agent, or change stored content.
outcome: The selected exact string record or complete version-number history.
effects: Reads the selected private database without writing it. CLI usage recording is separate and best effort.
authority: Bazaar owns stored bytes and version identity. Callers own ID meaning, content interpretation, and execution.
success: The requested record or history is returned without modifying Bazaar state.
failure_and_recovery: Missing or unsupported state and unknown IDs or versions are explicit errors. Reads never create a replacement database. Inspect the selected path and initialization state.
privacy: Content can contain private prompts or settings. Get discloses that exact content to its caller. History contains only the ID and version numbers.
does_not_authorize: Executing content, changing a caller's model or permissions, appending versions, or publishing private strings.
